Exercise A

A Tale of Two Cities

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

The Lowlands are home to Scotland's two largest and most famous cities: Glasgow and Edinburgh. Although they are only about 75 kilometres apart, the two cities have very different characters.

Edinburgh, which is the capital of Scotland, is known for its dramatic skyline. Edinburgh Castle, which sits on top of an extinct volcano, looks down over the old town. Every August the city hosts the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, which is the largest arts festival in the world. Visitors who come for the festival can see thousands of shows in just a few weeks.

Glasgow, which lies to the west, was once a great industrial city where ships were built and sent all over the world. Today it is a lively cultural centre that is famous for its music scene and friendly people. The people who live in Glasgow, sometimes called "Glaswegians", are known for their warm sense of humour.

Both cities have excellent universities that attract students from around the world. For many people who visit Scotland, these two Lowland cities are the highlight of the whole trip.

Exercise C

Combining Sentences

Choose the correct relative word to join the two ideas into one sentence.

Join the Ideas

1 Edinburgh is beautiful. It is the capital.
→ Edinburgh, is the capital, is beautiful.

2 This is the man. His dog won the prize.
→ This is the man dog won the prize.

3 Glasgow has a music scene. It is famous.
→ Glasgow has a music scene is famous.

4 The students come from abroad. They study here.
→ The students study here come from abroad.

5 August is the month. The festival happens then.
→ August is the month the festival happens.

6 The castle is a symbol. Tourists love it.
→ The castle, tourists love, is a symbol.

7 Ships were built there. The city grew rich.
→ The city ships were built grew rich.

8 She is the writer. She lived nearby.
→ She is the writer lived nearby.

Exercise D

Writing – A Tale of Two Places

Write a text (100–130 words) comparing two cities or places you know that are very different from each other. Use at least three relative clauses (who, which, where, whose).
